newsitem.title: UK: Botched EMU could drive up sterling -- UK's Major.
newsitem.headline: Botched EMU could drive up sterling -- UK's Major.

text.p: Sterling could rise to damagingly high levels if the European Union sets up a flawed single currency, Prime Minister John Major said on Tuesday.

Speaking on a campaign trip to a school, Major said capital would flow into strong currencies such as sterling and the Swiss Franc if economic and monetary union went ahead in the wrong circumstances.
This would wreak havoc on Britain's exporters, such as BMW's Rover subsidiary.
"Go down the road to Rover and ask them if they would sell their cars if they had an artificially high rate of sterling," Major told reporters.
For this and other reasons it was vital for Britain to keep its options open about whether to join the single currency.
"There are very practical reasons why, whether we go in or whether we stay out, it is imperative in the British national interest that we are in those negotiations," Major said.
